extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers, peer review mentors, NHMRC staff and other participants in the NHMRC Investigator Grants 2025 peer review process
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for conducting independent peer review of NHMRC Investigator Grants 2025 applications, including standards for assessment, conflict of interest disclosure, scoring, and special considerations (e.g., Indigenous health, relative to opportunity, industry experience).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness (NHMRC Principles of Peer Review)
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review processes are fair and seen to be fair by all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fairness is a high-level principle that underpins all NHMRC peer review processes (see Appendix A for additional detail). Peer reviewers must act in good faith and in NHMRC's and the research community's best interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency (NHMRC Principles of Peer Review)
rubrics_metrics.description: Transparency applies to all stages of peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Processes, decisions and relevant information should be transparent where appropriate; additional detail is provided in Appendix A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence (NHMRC Principles of Peer Review)
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers provide independent advice; there is independent oversight (Chairs, Peer Review Mentors, Observers where relevant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must give independent assessments; NHMRC assigns oversight roles to ensure independence is maintained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness and balance (NHMRC Principles of Peer Review)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is appropriate experience, expertise and representation of peer reviewers assessing applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NHMRC aims to assign reviewers with suitable expertise and to achieve balanced representation across relevant dimensions (field, career stage, perspectives).

rubrics_metrics.name: Research community participation (NHMRC Principles of Peer Review)
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons holding taxpayer-funded grants should willingly make themselves available to participate in peer review processes where possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation is an expectation under the Funding Agreement; peer reviewers should make themselves available whenever possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality (NHMRC Principles of Peer Review)
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants must respect confidentiality as important to fairness and robustness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NHMRC will endeavour to protect reviewer identity; reviewers must not disclose or misuse application contents; see Freedom of Information considerations for exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality (NHMRC Principles of Peer Review)
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review is objective and impartial with appropriate processes to manage disclosures of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must avoid bias, disclose interests, and follow NHMRC COI processes (Appendix B) to maintain impartiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality and excellence (NHMRC Principles of Peer Review)
rubrics_metrics.description: NHMRC will continue to introduce evidence-based improvements to achieve high-quality decision-making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should assess research quality rigorously and consistently using NHMRC criteria and score descriptors (Appendix C).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct per Australian Code for the Responsible Conduct of Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers participating in peer review must act in a way that is 'fair, rigorous and timely and maintains the confidentiality of the content'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should consult the Code and supporting guidance (Peer Review: A guide supporting the Australian Code) to understand expected behaviours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on inputting application content into generative AI
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers must not input any part of a grant application, or any information from it, into natural language processing and/or AI systems to assist assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prohibition is per NHMRC's Policy on Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Grant Applications and Peer Review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'interest' and legal disclosure obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Interests (material personal interests) must be dealt with consistently and disclosed in accordance with sections 16A/16B of the PGPA Rule 2014 and section 29 of the PGPA Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The obligation to disclose is ongoing; 'interest' and 'material personal interest' are treated interchangeably for the purposes of these guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest (CoI) identification and domains
rubrics_metrics.description: A CoI exists where there is divergence between professional responsibilities and personal interests; interests may fall into domains (involvement with application, working/professional/social relationships, collaborations, teaching/supervisory relationships, financial interests, other relevant relationships).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognise that many researchers will have unavoidable conflicts; disclose and let NHMRC determine conflict level. Appendix B provides potential CoI situations and guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory disclosure of interests in writing
rubrics_metrics.description: After appointment and before assessing applications, peer reviewers must disclose interests in writing (including dates substantiating collaborations). New interests must be disclosed at any stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declarations must include month/year for collaborations; NHMRC will determine conflict level. High CoI excludes reviewer from participating in that application's review (though they may provide scientific advice if requested).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for failure to disclose an interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to disclose an interest without a reasonable excuse will result in termination of the peer reviewer’s appointment under section 44B of the NHMRC Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer reviewers are encouraged to consult the secretariat if uncertain about disclosure matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom of Information considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: NHMRC is subject to the Freedom of Information Act 1982; where FoI requests cover peer review documents the process includes consultation and exemptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NHMRC will endeavour to protect reviewer identity within FoI constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaints handling and NHMRC enquiries
rubrics_metrics.description: NHMRC handles complaints, objections and requests for clarification about the peer review process and may contact peer reviewers for additional information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Further information on complaints is on the NHMRC website; reviewers should cooperate with enquiries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment against Investigator Grant assessment criteria and score descriptors (Appendix C)
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications are assessed against the Investigator Grant assessment criteria and associated score descriptors in Appendix C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer reviewers must use the score descriptors when scoring, consider Level applied for, Category/Level justification, career disruptions, relative to opportunity (Appendix G), and NHMRC Policy and Priorities where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track record assessment (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess an applicant's track record of research productivity and professional contribution 'relative to opportunity', considering career stage and circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should focus on quality and contribution rather than quantity; publication track record assessment should emphasise impact and contribution not journal metrics; ignore additional track record information in Career Context field that is outside permitted content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative to Opportunity and career disruption
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers must assess productivity relative to opportunity and take into account career circumstances and defined career disruptions when assessing track record and eligibility for Emerging Leadership (EL).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Career circumstances include research roles, resources, professional responsibilities, personal circumstances (disability, caring, Aboriginal/Torres Strait Islander community obligations), relocations, calamities; career disruption is a continuous absence of ≥90 calendar days (or equivalent long-term part-time) and can extend the 10-year eligibility/assessment timeframes proportionally. See Appendix G for full policy and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigating bias in peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers should be aware of unconscious bias (gender, ethnicity, nationality, employer, discipline) and take actions to minimise unintended systematic biases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NHMRC recommends DoRA guidance and encourages reviewers to undertake the Harvard Implicit Association Test (IAT) for gender and science to increase awareness (NHMRC does not access IAT results). Reviewers must follow all peer review principles and NHMRC materials on bias awareness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry-relevant experience recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers are to recognise and appropriately evaluate applicants' industry-relevant skills, experience and outputs as part of track record assessment and allow for time spent in commercialisation/industry as relative-to-opportunity considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix H provides a Guide to Evaluating Industry-Relevant Experience including examples of outputs across Advanced/Intermediate/Preliminary levels (IP, clinical trials/regulatory, industry participation, collaboration, start-ups, product-to-market indicators). Reviewers should value translation and commercial outputs that may have reduced traditional academic outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on use of journal impact factors and similar metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not appropriate to use publication metrics such as journal impact factors when assessing publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track record assessment should take account of field-specific publishing/citation practices and focus on overall impact, quality and contribution. Applicant-included journal-based metrics should not be taken into consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of the publication component of track record
rubrics_metrics.description: When assessing publications, focus on creativity and innovation of ideas, rigour of experimental design, appropriate statistical methods, reproducibility, analytical strength of interpretations and significance of outcomes as surrogates for research quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ignore publication-explanation content if it is not directly linked to the nominated publication or falls outside publications criteria (e.g., career publication metrics). Use field expertise to judge significance and contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhancing reproducibility and applicability of research outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers should consider how proposed and prior research enhances reproducibility and the applicability of outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is part of assessing research quality and translation potential; reviewers should look for transparent reporting, open science practices and other indicators of reproducibility (NHMRC encourages research quality guidelines such as the Hong Kong Principles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Research integrity issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers must be alert to potential research integrity concerns in applications and follow NHMRC guidance if issues are identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If integrity concerns arise, follow NHMRC processes (Appendices/Policy) and consult NHMRC staff; such issues may affect assessment or eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact between peer reviewers and applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance exists regarding contact between reviewers and applicants (see section 4.3.6.8).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must follow NHMRC rules on communications with applicants — generally avoid contact that could compromise independence and disclose any relevant interactions; consult NHMRC staff if uncertain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum number of independent assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: NHMRC will aim to obtain five independent assessments for each application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer reviewers provide independent written scores and feedback; NHMRC aggregates multiple assessments to create ranked lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant feedback requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers must summarise strengths and weaknesses of the application against each assessment criterion as applicant feedback, and remain fair and impartial when providing feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feedback will be provided to applicants de-identified after assessments are complete; reviewers must ensure comments are appropriate and not inappropriate (NHMRC staff review feedback for inappropriate comments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring, weighting, ranking and funding recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers enter scores per assessment criterion; NHMRC uses reviewers' criterion scores to calculate overall scores (arithmetically to three decimal places, accounting for criterion weighting) to create ranked lists for funding recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overall scores are calculated automatically; NHMRC conducts QA including outlier screening and may seek clarification from reviewers about score/comment discrepancies. Changes to rank-list preparation to support gender diversity do not affect how reviewers should assess applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statements of Expectations and Category/Level justification (applicant Level suitability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must justify their selected Category and Level; reviewers should consider this justification when assessing track record and may apply score adjustments or benchmarking if an applicant appears to have applied at an inappropriate Level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix F and F(i) contain Statements of Expectations and guidance. Table 1 provides suggested score adjustment approaches (benchmark against other assigned applicants at the Level you consider appropriate; consider +/- one score in some cases). Knowledge gain scoring should not be affected by Level mismatch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of applications with an Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander health focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications specifically relating to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander health will be identified and must have at least 20% research effort and/or capacity building focused on Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander health; they are assessed against the Indigenous Research Excellence Criteria (Appendix D).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NHMRC will endeavour to obtain at least one external assessment from an Indigenous health expert; Indigenous health reviewers provide guiding comments (may also be invited to score). Peer reviewers must consider Indigenous Research Excellence assessments when scoring Investigator Grant criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of Indigenous health research peer reviewers and community observers
rubrics_metrics.description: Indigenous health research peer reviewers assess adherence to Indigenous Research Excellence Criteria and provide guidance; community observers monitor procedural adherence and advise NHMRC on consistency and fairness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indigenous reviewers are not required to score (but may be invited). Observers do not participate in scoring and must advise NHMRC of conflicts and process concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Briefing, mentoring and responsibilities of Peer Review Mentors (PRMs)
rubrics_metrics.description: PRMs mentor peer reviewers on process, ensure consistency with score descriptors, consider relative to opportunity and Indigenous criteria, and respond to reviewer enquiries about process (PRMs do not assess applications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PRMs must familiarise themselves with the guidelines and assist with training; reviewers may seek PRM clarification on process during assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of additional research quality frameworks (DoRA, Hong Kong Principles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are encouraged to follow DoRA and Hong Kong Principles recommendations for responsible assessment, focusing on responsible research practices, transparent reporting, open science and recognition of diverse contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These frameworks inform not using journal metrics and emphasise research quality hallmarks as assessment surrogates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation, QA and outlier handling
rubrics_metrics.description: NHMRC staff review applicant feedback for inappropriate comments and perform checks to identify potential outlier scores; documentation of peer review assessments is retained for QA and potential enquiries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NHMRC will screen for discrepancies between scores and comments, seek clarifications, and may escalate issues as needed. Reviewers must complete scores and feedback by due dates.
